subject: MSA redlines — proposed joint-notice & contribution language
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — quick clarifying Q on notice + costs

Jordan — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per follow-up, attaching the redline we discussed. Two quick items your procurement counsel asked us to confirm before we exchange final language: 

1) Notice window: our standard is a 30-day notice-to-cure for IP third-party claims, with a separate 10-business-day operational notice for takedown requests. Can you confirm whether Aurelia is comfortable with that split, or whether you need a single consolidated notice window?

2) Contribution to defense costs: we proposed a mutual-contribution approach where each party bears its own outside counsel costs unless one party controls the defense. If Aurelia insists on a mandatory cost-sharing formula, could you confirm the percentage split range your team expects (we can be flexible for strategic customers)?

Putting Mina and Kimberly (legal) on cc to propose clean language. If you prefer, we can route a short joint-notice snippet for Aurelia counsel to mark up directly.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20m call if that speeds things up.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attach: Aurelia_Redline_MSA_v3.pdf (redline)
From: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@aureliatx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts (Aurelia Therapeutics) <contracts@aureliatx.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 12:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — quick clarifying Q on notice + costs

Ben — thanks, received. Short answers from the Aurelia side: 

- Notice window: procurement would prefer a single notice period (45 days) to simplify internal routing — operational teams can't easily split takedown vs infringement routing in our contract system. Is 45 days workable?

- Contribution: Aurelia's counsel is asking for a fallback split if costs are not apportioned by fault. They suggested a 60/40 split (party alleging infringement pays 60%) as a starting point because of our regulatory reporting constraints. That said, they're open to joint defense when control is expressly transferred.

I'll let our contracts team review the redline and return a markup early next week. Appreciate the offer to produce a snippet — that would help.

Jordan Hayes
VP, Legal & Ops, Aurelia Therapeutics
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — quick clarifying Q on notice + costs

Thanks Ben / Jordan (for the early guidance). Kimberly — quick internal note before we send a snippet to Aurelia's counsel: 

- 45-day single notice is longer than our default operational SLOs — it's OK for enterprise customers but increases exposure. If we accept 45 days we should: (a) narrow the proof/evidence window to require the claimant to provide supporting evidence at notice; and (b) keep an express right to suspend access for suspected infringement pending investigation.

- Contribution split: 60/40 tilt to claimant is aggressive for us. Proposed compromise: if the customer seeks a fixed split we can accept 60/40 only where the claimant both (i) controls the notice and (ii) has access to supplier-provided logs/evidence that demonstrate the alleged use. Otherwise, default to joint-defense (each pays own counsel) unless control is transferred.

I'll draft two short options: (1) 45-day single notice + evidence requirement + suspension right; (2) 30/10 split (notice/takedown) with joint-defense default but optional 60/40 if customer provides evidence and elects to control defense. Ben — which option do you want me to present to Aurelia?

— Mina
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — quick clarifying Q on notice + costs

Mina — good outline. I drafted a short, customer-friendly snippet that tries to preserve our operational rights while accepting Aurelia's preference for a single notice period. Key points: 45-day consolidated notice; claimant must include (i) alleged infringing content with timestamps; (ii) sample logs or prompts sufficient to triage; Redwood may suspend access to the affected tenant or model variant for 7 business days pending reasonable investigation; where Aurelia elects to control defense, we will negotiate a cost-sharing arrangement (not automatic 60/40). If we get pushback, the fallback is a precise 60/40 clause but only tied to narrow conditions (control + evidence access).

I'll attach the snippet and a redlined MSA paragraph. Recommend we send both options to Aurelia: the customer-friendly consolidated 45-day + evidence approach, and the joint-defense default with the 30/10 operational split (our preference).

-Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attach: proposed-joint-notice-snippet.docx (text snippet)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Contracts (Aurelia Therapeutics) <contracts@aureliatx.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — proposed joint-notice options & next steps

Jordan — attaching two short options as promised (snippet + redline). Quick summary in-line so your counsel can pick: 

Option A (customer-friendly): consolidated 45-day notice; claimant provides supporting timestamps and sample logs; Redwood reserved right to suspend access for up to 7 business days pending investigation; cost allocation: joint-defense unless Aurelia elects to control defense and then parties negotiate cost-sharing.

Option B (Redwood-preferred): split 30-day infringement notice / 10-business-day operational takedown; joint-defense default (each party pays its own counsel) unless control is transferred, in which case a negotiated cost-share applies; more protective suspension language and clearer evidence-handover obligations.

Next steps: please have contracts review and tell us which option they prefer or provide edits; if Aurelia wants the 60/40 fallback, can you ask them to specify the triggering mechanics (control + proof) so we can accept a narrow, conditional 60/40 clause rather than a blanket allocation.

Happy to jump on a 20m call with contracts if that helps — Mina and Kimberly will be on the line to expedite.

Best,
Ben
Attachments: Aurelia_Redline_MSA_v3.pdf (redline), proposed-joint-notice-snippet.docx (text snippet)
From: Contracts (Aurelia Therapeutics) <contracts@aureliatx.com>

Cc: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@aureliatx.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 16:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — proposed joint-notice options & next steps

Ben / team — thanks for the two options and the clear summaries. Our counsel prefers Option A (45-day consolidated notice) but with an explicit evidence-preservation clause and a mechanism for expedited access to logs under NDA. Regarding cost allocation: Aurelia is prepared to accept joint-defense for the initial period but asks that a 60/40 split be available as a fallback if (i) Aurelia controls the defense and (ii) Redwood is unwilling to share forensic logs within 10 business days. We will circulate a quick markup that adds an evidence-preservation paragraph and clarifies the logs NDA (we're attaching our redline later today).

Jordan Hayes
VP, Legal & Ops, Aurelia Therapeutics

---
On behalf of Contracts: we will aim to return the redline by EOD Wednesday; if Redwood agrees to the 10-business-day forensic logs SLA under NDA, Aurelia will drop the unconditional 60/40 ask and accept the negotiated fallback approach.

Contracts Team
Aurelia Therapeutics
